newsitem.title: UK: ISO sees sugar prices holding in range to September.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees sugar prices holding in range to September.

text.p: World raw sugar prices are likely to hold in a range between 10 and 12 cents/lb until the end of the current October/September cycle, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Friday.
This assumed neutral weather conditions for the remaining months of the 1996/97 cycle, it said.
"In the near term, prices should remain under pressure. The fundamentals...remain bearish," it said in its latest review of the world market situation.
White sugar prices were expected to remain in a range between 12.5 to 14.5 cents/lb.
"It can also be expected that prices may drift towards the low limit of the range after the expiration of the July 1997 (raws) futures contract," the ISO said.
July was the last position against which sugar from the current crop cycle can be priced, it noted.
July raws are trading on the New York market at between 10.75 and 10.90 cents/lb, while August whites are trading in London between $311 and $313.
The ISO said exports in two exporters with record crops -- Brazil and Thailand -- were running significantly behind last year.
Both nations would want to clear their stocks before sugar started to flow in quantity from the new crops -- Brazil in July and Thailand in December.
